description: Mutations in human GBA1 (glucosidase, beta, acid 1) can cause Gaucher disease, an autosomal recessive lysosomal (lipid) storage disease, and have been associated with late onset Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia. These mice express the mutant D427V Gba1 protein, which corresponds to the D409V mutation in the mature human GBA1 protein, and possess loxP sites flanking exons 6 through 8. Mice that are heterozygous for the targeted mutation are viable and fertile. Homozygous Gba1 D409V knock-in mice show a significant reduction in Gba1 protein level and glucocerebrosidase activity, and a significant increase in glucosylsphingosine in both brain and liver tissues. Heterozygotes demonstrate significant cognitive impairment by the age of 12 months, as determined by both Morris water maze and Y-maze behavioral tests (PMID: 31299418). When these mutant mice are bred to mice that express Cre recombinase, resulting offspring will have exons 6 through 8 deleted in the cre-expressing tissues and will no longer express the mutant D427V protein. Preliminary characterization was presented in a poster at the 2015 Society for Neuroscience conference. Read More

development: A targeting vector containing a FRT site flanked NEO cassette, and a F3 FRT site flanked PurO cassette was used to introduce the D427V point mutation into exon 10. The FRT site flanked NEO cassette was inserted into intron 5 and the F3 FRT site flanked PurO cassette was inserted into intron 8. In addition, loxP sites were inserted to flank exons 6 through 8. The construct was electroporated into C57BL/6NTac derived Art B6 3.6 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into BALB/c blastocysts. The resulting chimeric animals were crossed to FLP recombinase expressing females on the C57BL/6NTac background, C57BL/6NTac-Tg(CAG-Flpe)2Art, to remove the selection cassettes (see SNP results below). These mice no longer carry the FLP recombinase allele. Upon arrival at The Jackson Laboratory, the mice were crossed to C57BL/6N (Stock No. 005304) at least once to establish the colony. A 32 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 27 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the rederived living colony at The Jackson Laboratory Repository. While the 27 markers throughout the genome suggested a C57BL/6 genetic background, 4 of 5 markers that determine C57BL/6J from C57BL/6N were found to be segregating. These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository were on a mixed C57BL/6J ; C57BL/6N genetic background. These data showed ~97-99% C57BL/6 markers (~89-92% C57BL/6J ; ~7-8% C57BL/6NCrl). Of note, the same 2 males were also tested using our routine 48 SNP panel (43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains). description: LRRK2 (leucine rich repeat kinase 2) protein contains a kinase domain where both the N2081D Crohn's disease (CD) risk and the G2019S Parkinson's disease (PD)-pathogenic variants are located. Lrrk2N2081D knock-in mice express the conserved N2081D LRRK2 variant, which is expressed at endogenous levels. Homozygotes show increased sensitivity to chemically-induced colitis. No pathological
phenotype: has been observed in untreated mice, however there is an increase in phosphorylated RAB10 (RAB10, member RAS oncogene family) protein levels in the tissues of these mice compared to wildtype. Rab10 encodes a key substrate for LRRK2. Colitis is induced by administering 2% dextran sodium sulfate (DSS) in the drinking water of 16-week-old homozygous male and female mice for 8 days, followed by 3 days of regular water for partial recovery. In both sexes, homozygous mice exhibit more severe weight loss compared to wildtype animals. A significant number of males require early sacrifice due to the severity of colitis symptoms. At the experimental end point, both male and female mice have shorter colons than their sex-matched wildtype counterparts, indicating a greater degree of colonic inflammation. Stool samples extracted from colons of N2081D mutation carriers have significantly higher levels of the proinflammatory marker lipocalin-2 (LCN2). Male N2081D carriers also have increased spleen weight compared to wildtype mice, suggesting a heightened immune response. Histological examination of colon samples reveals a greater degree of inflammation and tissue damage in both male and female Lrrk2N2081D carriers compared to sex-matched wildtype mice. Collectively, results show that the Lrrk2N2081D mutation significantly exacerbates colonic inflammation and the severity of induced colitis, validating the Lrrk2N2081D model as a tool to study Lrrk2-linked Crohn's disease pathogenic mechanisms. Studies suggest that the N2081D mutation activates LRRK2 by inducing a conformational shift, resulting in functional effects distinct from the Parkinson's disease-associated LRRK2 G2019S variant. development: The LRRK2 flox-R1441G knock-in allele was designed to incorporate a conditional R1441G point mutation into exon 31 of the leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (Lrrk2) gene based on the NCBI transcript NM_025730.3 (Ensembl transcript ENSMUST00000060642). The targeting vector, which was inserted into the endogenous Lrrk2 intron 30, consists of an initial loxP site, followed by an FRT-flanked neomycin cassette, exons 31-51 Lrrk2 cDNA including the 3' untranslated region (UTR), an hGHpA (2.1 kb of the human growth hormone gene harboring the hGH polyadenylation signal), an F3-flanked puromycin cassette, and a second loxP site. Genomic exon 31 harboring the R1441G mutation is located immediately downstream of the second loxP site. The target construct was electroporated into C57BL/6N-derived embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into recipient blastocysts. The resulting chimeric mice were bred to FLP-recombinase mice, on a C57BL/6N background, to remove the FRT-flanked neomycin cassette and the F3-flanked puromycin cassette. The donating laboratory reported they maintained this mouse line on a C57BL/6N background prior to sending homozygous males to The Jackson Laboratory in 2025. Upon arrival, sperm was cryopreserved. To establish our live colony, an aliquot of frozen sperm was used to fertilize C57BL/6NJ (Stock No. 005304) oocytes. In 2025, a 48 SNP (single nucleotide polymorphism) panel analysis, with 43 markers covering all 19 chromosomes and the X chromosome, as well as 5 markers that distinguish between the C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N substrains, was performed on the homozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory. All markers were C57BL/6N allele-type. In 2025, the homozygous males sent to The Jackson Laboratory were used to freeze sperm. Samples from those males were analyzed via the miniMUGA 10,000 SNP panel. This showed 98.6-100% of the markers as C57BL/6. The scoring algorithm was unable to discern the C57BL/6 substrain with any certainty. Additionally, one mouse was identified potentially having markers other than C57BL/6 present on Chromosome 19 ~45.45-46.8 Mb (this was not examined further). These data suggest the mice sent to The Jackson Laboratory were on a C57BL/6 genetic background. development: To generate the PAC-Tg(SNCAA53T) transgene, the 146 kb RPCI-1 human male P1 artificial chromosome (PAC) clone 27M07, containing the entire human SNCA (synuclein, alpha (non A4 component of amyloid precursor)) gene and 34 kb of its upstream region, was modified to have the A53T human mutation associated with autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease (G>A substitution at base 420 of the cDNA sequence). This transgene was microinjected into the pronuclei of fertilized FVB/N ova. Each transgenic founder mouse was bred to FVB/N wildtype mice to generate the individual founder lines (1 and 2). Each PAC-Tg(SNCAA53T) transgenic line was independently maintained as coisogenic on the FVB/N genetic background by
breeding: together as homozygotes. To generate the Snca knock-out allele, a targeting vector was designed to replace exons 4 and 5 with a reverse-oriented neomycin resistance cassette (PGK-neo from the vector pPNT). The construct was electroporated into 129S6/SvEvTac-derived TC-1 embryonic stem (ES) cells. Correctly targeted ES cells were injected into recipient blastocysts and the resulting mutant mice were generated and maintained as coisogenic on the 129S6/SvEvTac genetic background. To generate the dbl-PAC-Tg(SNCAA53T);Snca-/- strain, homozygous PAC-Tg(SNCAA53T) line 1 mice (FVB/N genetic background) were bred with mice homozygous for the Snca knock-out allele (129S6/SvEvTac genetic background). Similarly, PAC-Tg(SNCAA53T) line 2 homozygotes were bred with Snca knock-out mice. These two mutant strains were then intercrossed and bred to homozygosity to create the double transgenic strain. In 2010, homozygous mice [dbl-PAC-Tg(SNCAA53T);Snca-/-] were originally reported to carry four insertions of the PAC-Tg(SNCAA53T) transgene; two for the line 1 insert on chromosome 3 and two for the line 2 insert on chromosome 14 [see Detailed Description section for 2022 updated information regarding the transgene insertion sites, copy number and complexity (genomic duplication/rearrangement, co-integration with multiple genomic fragments)]. This double transgenic strain was maintained on a mixed FVB/N;129S6/SvEvTac background using multiple breeding units without repeated brother-sister matings: thus the only portions of the FVB/N or 129S6/SvEvTac genomes fixed in these mice are the FVB/N regions flanking the PAC-Tg(SNCAA53T) transgene insertion sites and the 129S6/SvEvTac regions around the Snca knock-out allele. The dbl-PAC-Tg(SNCAA53T);Snca-/- mice were sent to The Jackson Laboratory Repository. Upon arrival, mice were bred together to establish the colony. description: There are several challenges facing researchers who are developing antibody-based therapeutics, including assessing half-life, selecting efficacious variants, and determining dosage for clinical trials. The mechanism behind IgG's extended half-life lies in the interaction between IgG and the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), encoded by Fcgrt, Fc receptor, IgG, alpha chain transporter (Roopenian et al., 2003; Challa et al., 2014). Standard rodent models are problematic in that mouse and rat FcRn do not bind human IgG with the same affinity as human FcRn, leading to inaccurate half-life data (Ober et al., 2001). Tg32 (Stock No. 014565) and Tg276 (Stock No. 004919) are humanized mouse models that can be used to predict the pharmacokinetics (PK) of IgG antibodies in humans with an accuracy comparable to non-human primates (NHPs). Both carry a knock-out mutation for the mouse Fcgrt gene (Stock No. 003982) in addition to a transgene expressing the human FCGRT gene either under the control of its own native promoter (Stock No. 014565) or under the control of the more broadly-expressed CAG promoter (human cytomegalovirus (CMV) enhancer fused to the chicken beta-actin; Stock No. 004919). description: MS-NASH (formerly called FATZO) is an inbred polygenic mouse model for studying obesity, metabolic syndrome and diabetes - all in the presumed presence of an intact leptin pathway. On standard diet, MS-NASH males exhibit obesity in a pre-diabetic state that slowly progresses to overt diabetes. MS-NASH females exhibit obesity but do not develop any diabetic
phenotype: . Approximately ~95% of MS-NASH males become obese (30 grams) by 8 weeks of age. Male obesity is progressive, but not as severe as mice with non-functioning leptin signaling pathways. Glucose intolerance with increased insulin levels is reported in MS-NASH males as young as 6 weeks of age. MS-NASH males become hyperglycemic at ~14 weeks of age, rapidly develop insulin resistance and become hyperinsulinemic (insulin secretion remains at high levels). The early hyperglycemia of MS-NASH males can be accelerated by high fat diets. Furthermore, MS-NASH males maintained on a western diet with fructose develop liver steatosis leading to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, or MASH (formerly called NAFLD/NASH). Upon administration of the GLP-1 agonist semaglutide, MS-NASH males respond with a reduction in body weight, food intake and blood glucose. Additional metabolic phenotypes expected from the JAX MSNASH/PcoJ model can be viewed here. Additional characterization of the MS-NASH inbred strain may be available at the Crown Biosciences - Rodent Models of NASH website. The observed coat color is similar to that of C57BL/6J, but there is a small range in coat color from dark brown to black. Read More

description: These NSG-MHC I/II DKO mice are also called NSG-(KbDb)null (IA)null or NSG-(Kb Db)null (IAnull) in Brehm et al. 2019 FASEB J [PMID:30383447]. These mice are NOD.scid;IL2rg-deficient (NSG) animals also containing null targeted mutations for mouse MHC class I genes (H2-K1 and H2-D1) and a TALEN-made null mutation for the mouse class II gene (H2-Ab1 [I-A]) - making them an MHC I/II double knock-out. These NSG-MHC I/II DKO mice combine the features of the severe combined immune deficiency mutation or scid (B and T cell deficiency), IL2 receptor gamma chain deficiency (NK cell deficiency), MHC class I molecule deficiency (H2-K and D), and MHC class II molecule deficiency (IA). Mice homozygous for the five mutations are viable, normal in size and do not display any gross physical or behavioral abnormalities. These mice exhibit a significantly delayed onset of xenogeneic GvHD compared to NSG mice. The rate and severity of onset is highly dependent on preparatory irradiation dose (or absence), specific donor used, and cell dose injected. Each PBMC donor requires a pilot engraftment using more than one cell dose to determine the overall engraftment characteristics. Once established, these engraftment characteristics are highly reproducible. At JAX, the survival of non-irradiated mice injected with 10 x 106 human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) is greater than 100 days, with 13/15 of mice exhibiting no symptoms of GVHD for up to 125 days. Because this strain carries a null mutation in the MHC class I H2-Ab1 gene rather than β-2M, IgG clearance is similar to that observed in the NSG model. This strain may be useful to study human immunity in the absence of GVHD and to evaluate antibody-based therapeutics. Stock No. 025216 may be prone to aggressive behavior, including whisker picking, barbering and biting [June 2025]. To help mitigate this, we suggest that, upon receiving the mice, researchers add enrichment items (e.g., a Shepherd Shack) and reduce housing density. Read More
